domain: environmental regulation / referral screening outcome prediction
prediction_question: For a development referred under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (EPBC Act), at the instant the referral is validated and published on the EPBC Act Public Portal (with its title, proponent, industry type, location and primary jurisdiction visible), will the delegate's referral decision (due within 20 business days of validation) declare the action a controlled action (requiring formal assessment and approval) rather than 'not a controlled action' or 'not a controlled action - particular manner'? Prospective users: proponents and their environmental consultants (screening and budgeting for assessment before lodging), and oversight researchers studying what drives regulatory thresholds. A useful prediction prices assessment risk at referral time instead of waiting the ~4 weeks for the decision.
prediction_time: Instant = the referral's validation/publication on the EPBC Act Public Portal (per-project pages show a stage timeline Lodgement -> Validation -> Referral Decision -> Assessment -> Final Decision; the portal's list carries a 'Valid Date' column). Features fixed at that instant: project title, proponent name, industry type, location (address string and primary jurisdiction), and referral document metadata. The referral decision (the label) is published later on the same project page as a decision notice, within the statutory 20-business-day window - the outcome cannot exist at the instant.
target_definition: Binary: 1 if the referral decision declares a controlled action (assessment approach determined on the project page; decision notice 'Controlled Action'), 0 for 'Not a controlled action' / 'particular manner' decisions. Label source = the per-project decision field/notice on the portal, excludable from shipped features (features are referral-time fields only). Population: all referrals in the portal's All-referrals list; still-open referrals at the data edge are censored, not imputed.

Per-project summary pages ARE static-fetchable anonymously (project-referral-summary/?id=..., ~236 KB, carries EPBC number, status, stage timeline).

split_strategy: Not yet computed - depends on measured referral volumes and outcome vocabulary. Prior expectation (labelled as such, not measured): ~500-800 referrals/year since 2000, controlled-action share historically a large minority (decisive construction measurement). Whether the portal's '5000 records' is the full historical population or a display cap is an OPEN measurement (grid XHR replay needed); per-year coverage must be established before split windows can be designed.

measurements.access_2026_10_28: Portal list: anonymous, JS-rendered PCF grid, 10 rows/page, '5000 records' shown; XHR-driven pagination not reproducible by plain urllib (grid endpoint guesses 404); static per-project pages fetch anonymously. One decided project page read anonymously: EPBC 2024/10023 (Princes Highway upgrade program - Milton Ulladulla bypass) status 'Assessment Approach Determined' with the full stage timeline rendered in static HTML. Extraction is therefore browser-automation shaped (grid pagination ~500 XHR calls + optional per-project pages), feasible on a worker with a headless browser; no bulk CSV/JSON channel was found in the bounded sweep.
measurements.portal_fields_2026_10_28: List row fields (verified in browser): EPBC Number, Project, Proposer/Approval Holder, Location, Industry Type, Valid Date, Project Status (observed value 'Referral Decision - Open for Public Comment'), Primary Jurisdiction. Whether the terminal referral-decision outcome is exposed in the LIST (status string) or only on per-project pages is unresolved - the label-derivation cost differs by an order of magnitude between the two.
measurements.ecosystem_note_2026_10_28: The EPBC Act is administered by Australia's National EPA (nationalepa.gov.au, portal still on environment.gov.au domain). No machine-readable bulk referral-decision dataset was found on data.gov.au in the bounded catalogue sweep (nearest: referrals spatial database, WMS-only).
measurements.population_2026_10_29: True population measured via the list's Valid Date From/To filters + Apply Filter (each filter is honored server-side and reports a true count; the unfiltered list is capped). Valid Date windows and 'N records found': 2000-01-01..2009-12-31 = 3,403; 2010-01-01..2019-12-31 = 3,067; 2020-01-01..2026-12-31 = 1,826; 2019 single year = 177. Sum over the three windows = 8,296 referrals since 2000, while the unfiltered list shows exactly '5000 records found' with 500 pages x 10 rows - the 5,000 is a confirmed portal display cap, not the population. Filters applied anonymously in the supported browser; counts read from the rendered 'records found' text.
measurements.list_grid_channel_2026_10_29: Grid mechanics confirmed: the PCF grid pages via POST /_services/entity-grid-data.json/2ab10dab-d681-4911-b881-cc99413f07b6 with an opaque base64SecureConfiguration body (captured by hooking XHR in page context), so pagination cannot be replayed with arbitrary offsets by a plain client; but the date filters + Apply Filter drive the same grid server-side and give true per-window counts. Row links expose per-project GUIDs: /all-referrals/project-referral-summary/?id=<guid>. An 'Export' button exists on the list; clicking it produced no download in a bounded attempt (2026-10-29), untested further.
measurements.label_channel_2026_10_29: The list's Project Status column carries project-level status, not the decision outcome. Vocabulary observed in filtered samples: 'Referral Decision - Open for Public Comment' (open), 'Referral Decision Made', 'Advice Not Required', 'Approval Decision made', 'Condition variation being considered', 'Project Withdrawn' - the list tells whether a decision exists and whether the referral was withdrawn (censored), but the controlled-action outcome itself is not in list rows. The per-project summary page is static-fetchable anonymously (223,247 bytes, 3.23 s, project 2019/8566) and renders the stage timeline (Lodgement -> Validation -> Referral Decision -> Assessment -> Final Decision -> Post Approval -> Completed), but the 'Decision notices' and 'Decisions related with this referral' sections load via XHR grids, so the decision value itself still needs the JS-rendered notices grid or the notice PDFs. Label-derivation cost would therefore be per-project (~8,296 projects) had the licence been clean.

rejection_reason: Licence class D: the only licence information linked from the referral register's own pages is the Online Services terms (https://onlineservices.environment.gov.au/terms-and-conditions, footer 'Terms and Conditions' link on the all-referrals list page and on per-project pages), which state: 'Subject to paragraph 2(b), you are prohibited from: reproducing Our Material; reselling or distributing Our Material; re-transmitting the Our Material by any medium of communication; uploading and/or reposting Our Material to any other site on the Internet' and 'You may access and download Our Material from the Portal solely for your own use'. No Creative Commons or other open licence appears anywhere in those terms (verified by text search of the full page). The publisher's general copyright notices (DCCEEW and National EPA, both read in the supported browser 2026-10-29) default to CC BY 4.0 'Unless otherwise specified' and expressly exclude content 'subject to ... some other licence terms'; the register's own pages specify those other terms. A derived benchmark would republish referral rows, so the source cannot ship. What would reopen: (a) the publisher issues an explicit open-licence instrument for the referral register itself (e.g. a data.gov.au catalogue record naming the register - not the WMS-only spatial sibling - under CC BY, or a written publisher statement that the Online Services terms do not govern the public register); or (b) the register becomes available through a channel whose terms permit redistribution (e.g. a bulk dataset on data.gov.au).
review: DROPPED on licence (2026-10-29), with population and access measurements preserved for any reopening. Contracts at close: (1) Redistribution FAILED - the only licence information linked from the register's own pages (list and per-project footers) is the Online Services terms that prohibit reproducing/distributing 'Our Material' and allow download 'solely for your own use'; the department's CC BY 4.0 default is expressly displaced by 'some other licence terms' and its own no-circumvention clause. Both scope readings of the linked terms fail: governed -> prohibited; not governed -> no instrument at all (unstated). (2) Prediction timing SUPPORTED in structure (validation instant, 20-business-day statutory decision window, decision published later on the same project page) - unchanged from 2026-10-28. (3) Target obtainable in principle but EXPENSIVE: the list carries decision-exists and withdrawn statuses only; the outcome needs per-project notice grids/PDFs (~8,296 projects measured). (4) Split capacity: population measured (3,403 referrals 2000-2009, 3,067 2010-2019, 1,826 2020-2026, 2019 = 177) - ample volume for disjoint windows had the label channel been open; outcome mix unmeasured (licence veto came first). (5) Contribution: novelty never run - the licence veto is decisive and cheaper; a reopened lead must still run check-novelty.py.
next_action: Closed. Reopen ONLY on new licence evidence: (a) an explicit open-licence instrument for the referral register from the publisher (data.gov.au catalogue record naming the register itself, or a written publisher statement that the Online Services terms do not govern the public register), or (b) the register published via a redistribution-permitting channel. On reopening, the 2026-10-29 measurements (population 8,296, cap 5,000, filter recipe, per-project GUID link pattern, status vocabulary, label-channel cost) remain valid access evidence; the decision-outcome channel (notices grid/PDFs) and the novelty search are the next probes. Do not extend this rejection to other DCCEEW/National EPA material where no restrictive terms are linked from the material itself.

jurisdiction.publisher: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water / National EPA (EPBC Act Public Portal)

licence_note: Class D (2026-10-29): the register's own pages link restrictive terms in their footer (Terms and Conditions -> https://onlineservices.environment.gov.au/terms-and-conditions, linked from BOTH the all-referrals list and per-project pages), and those terms prohibit reproducing and distributing 'Our Material' and permit download 'solely for your own use'. The department's general CC BY 4.0 copyright notice cannot override this: it applies 'Unless otherwise specified', excludes 'content that is specified as being subject to third party copyright limitations or some other licence terms', and its own 'No circumvention of terms' clause directs the user to comply with the licensing information for each set of material - which for this register is the restrictive instrument. Both scope readings fail the redistribution contract: (1) if the linked terms govern the portal, redistribution is prohibited; (2) if they do not, the register carries no licence instrument at all (unstated, class C posture, closed under standing policy). Neither reading permits publishing derived rows. Scope of this rejection: THIS portal's material only; it does not generalize to other DCCEEW/National EPA publications where no restrictive terms are linked from the material itself.
